symptoms: leaf: Necrotic streaks along the veins Interveinal chlorosis or yellowing Leaf deformation or curling Small necrotic spots or flecks on older leaves timing: Symptoms usually appear on older leaves but can affect leaves at all stages plant: Stunting Reduced seed quality in severe infections
description: Soybean vein necrosis virus (SVNV) is a tospovirus affecting soybean, causing necrosis along leaf veins and reducing plant vigor and seed quality.
management: cultural_control: Use pathogen-free seed Remove volunteer soybean and other host plants to reduce inoculum Avoid planting near areas with high thrips populations chemical_control: Insecticides targeting thrips may reduce virus spread genetic_control: No fully resistant soybean cultivars currently available; research ongoing
